title: Basic generator coefficient squares in semilinear systems
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$, $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For finite-type $k$-schemes $W$ use their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and $\widehat R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$. Use strict semilinear system categories $\mathscr S_W$, the adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ with actual unit $u$ and counit $e$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], and the simultaneous section constructions of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. The system operations are exact inverse image $P_v$, its derived right adjoint $S_v$, exact termwise open extension $J_j\dashv P_j$, and derived tensor. Maps $v$ are separated finite type, $p$ proper, and $j$ quasi-compact open [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Integral operations are completed pullback and completed tensor [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], proper direct image [def-weil-derived-direct-image], and localized completed-ring open extension [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison].

Take derived-complete constructible integral inputs. Restrict every input and intermediate system used below to normalized systems with compatible etale-origin witnesses, constructible cohomology, and cohomological and finite Tor amplitudes in common finite intervals [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. For each single basic operation $A$ let
$$d_A:\mathcal L A(\mathcal R K_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{\rm int}(K_i)$$
be the identification with its strict reduction-tower definition (two inputs for tensor); for $J_j$ use the specified $d_j$ of [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison]. Let $r_A:\mathcal R(A_{\rm int}(K_i))\to A(\mathcal R K_i)$ be the canonical coefficient comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction], with $r_j$ the preceding open comparison. Then, as actual semilinear-system maps,
$$r_A=e_{A(\mathcal R K_i)}\circ\mathcal R(d_A^{-1}).$$

For a word $B$ of at most three basic operations write $r_B$ for the successive composite of these comparisons, with the operation applied to the inner comparison in each slot. Let $\tau:B\to C$ be one basic structural generator: tensor associativity or its unit identification, pullback composition, a pullback/direct-image or open-adjunction unit or counit, direct-image composition, the canonical open base-change or open-tensor isomorphism [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], or one proper/open interchange [lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting]. The corresponding integral maps $\tau_{\rm int}$ are the canonical completed ringed-site maps, with proper/open interchange the open-adjunction transpose of inverse open restriction through the clopen component. Each generator has its two words of length at most three, counting tensor as a binary operation. Then its coefficient square commutes in the derived semilinear-system category:
$$\tau_{\mathcal R K_i}\circ r_B=r_C\circ\mathcal R(\tau_{\rm int}).$$
For proper/open interchange, the corresponding coefficient square for $\lambda_Q:P_iS_pJ_k\cong S_r$ commutes as well. Tensor and square identifications here are the canonical ringed-topos identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence]. No assertion about realizing arbitrary expression trees, arbitrary whiskering, nested compact-support functors, or detecting equality by evaluated derived arrows is part of this statement.

proof.text: Work in the simultaneous enhanced semilinear-section models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. The normalized hypotheses and the common constructibility, etale-origin, cohomological, and Tor bounds are exactly the domain restrictions in the statement, so every operation and every comparison occurring in a word of length at most three is represented by one actual derived-system transformation. The reduction/total-limit adjunction is the actual adjunction of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], with unit \(u\) and counit \(e\), and its unit/counit identities hold as identities of derived systems. In particular, all maps below are formed before applying \(\mathcal L\), finite evaluation, or restriction of scalars.

source.place: The sentence “The maps used here are tensor reassociation, evaluation, and adjunction units and counits...”

proof.text:
For one basic unary operation \(A\), and for tensor in its two input variables, write \(h_A=d_A^{-1}:A_{\rm int}(K_i)\to\mathcal L A(\mathcal R K_i)\). Under \(\mathcal R\dashv\mathcal L\) of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] the system map whose adjunct is \(h_A\) is \(e_{A(\mathcal R K_i)}\circ\mathcal R(h_A)\), by the triangle identities stated there. For pullback, tensor and proper direct image, \(d_A\) is the identity of models: [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] defines \(Lf^*K=R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_nf^*(P_n)\) and the completed tensor as \(R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(P_n\otimes Q_n)\) on flat-term K-flat representatives with \(P_n=P\otimes(A_n)_W\), and [def-weil-derived-direct-image] defines \(Rp_*K=R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRp_{*,n}(K_n)\); by [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] \(\mathcal R K\) is represented by the same tower \((P\otimes(A_n)_W)_n\) and \(\mathcal L=R\lim\circ U\) uses the same total-limit model, while the system operations evaluate to \(f^*\), \(\otimes\) and \(Rp_{*,n}\) [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. By the counit clause of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], level \(n\) of \(e_N\) is the scalar-extension adjoint of the total-limit projection \(\pi_n\); hence level \(n\) of \(e_{A(\mathcal RK_i)}\circ\mathcal R(h_A)\) is the scalar-extension adjoint \((A_{\rm int}K_i)\otimes^L(A_n)\to A(K_{i,n})\) of the \(n\)th limit projection. That is exactly the finite-reduction comparison of [def-weil-derived-direct-image] and the reduction comparison of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] for pullback and tensor, which are adjoint to the same projections. The system map \(r_A\) specified by the reduction construction is this adjunct, i.e. \(r_A=e_{A(\mathcal R K_i)}\circ\mathcal R(d_A^{-1})\); the identification is made through the adjunction, not by evaluating derived arrows. For \(J_j\) the formula is a computation: [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison] supplies \(r_j\) as a system map and \(d_j=u_{j_!K}^{-1}\circ\mathcal L(r_j)^{-1}\), so
\[
e_{J_j\mathcal R K}\circ\mathcal R(d_j^{-1})=e_{J_j\mathcal RK}\circ\mathcal R\mathcal L(r_j)\circ\mathcal R(u_{j_!K})=r_j\circ e_{\mathcal R j_!K}\circ\mathcal R(u_{j_!K})=r_j
\]
by naturality of \(e\) and the triangle identity \(e_{\mathcal RX}\circ\mathcal R(u_X)=1\). The two-input formula for tensor is the same argument in both variables. These equalities hold in the derived semilinear-system category and are natural in all inputs.

source.place: The sentence “The maps used here are tensor reassociation, evaluation, and adjunction units and counits, whose coefficient comparisons are proved in [lem-fix-operation-reduction].”

proof.text:
By Step 2 and the \(\mathcal R\dashv\mathcal L\) bijection on morphisms, the square \(\tau_{\mathcal R K_i}r_B=r_C\mathcal R(\tau_{\rm int})\) for a generator is equivalent to the statement that, under the strict reduction-tower identifications \(d\) of its factors, \(\tau_{\rm int}\) is \(\mathcal L(\tau_{\mathcal RK_i})\); here naturality of \(e\) moves the inner comparisons of \(r_B,r_C\) past the counit. For tensor associativity and its unit identifications, and for pullback composition, this is [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution]: under its counit identifications of completed pullback and completed tensor of limits with limits of the system operations (the identifications \(d\) of Step 2 on reduction systems), the associator and action unitors of completed tensor and the composition comparison of completed pullbacks are the limits of the corresponding canonical system maps, compatibly with substitution. For pullback/direct-image units and counits and direct-image composition, [lem-fix-operation-reduction] says that the reduction comparisons preserve the units and counits used to construct these transformations, and [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] says that the comparisons, the pullback-composition maps, the adjunction units and counits and their transposes (direct-image compositors being mates of pullback compositors) have simultaneous coherent models, and that composition and adjunction transposition preserve these constructions. Hence the transpose of the reduction comparison for \(S_v\) is the derived counit transpose on the same models, and pasting its naturality squares with the formula of Step 2 gives, for every tensor-associativity or unit generator, pullback-composition generator, pullback/direct-image unit or counit, and direct-image-composition generator,
\[
\tau_{\mathcal R K_i}r_B=r_C\mathcal R(\tau_{\rm int}).
\]
The canonical tensor and square identifications appearing in these pastings are compatible by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence]. Since \(B\) and \(C\) have length at most three, \(r_B,r_C\) contain finitely many factors, and ordinary bifunctoriality and naturality paste the one-factor squares to the displayed square without any faithfulness claim about evaluations.

source.place: The sentence “The maps used here are tensor reassociation, evaluation, and adjunction units and counits...”

proof.text: For the open generators, [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] gives the open unit identifications and states that its open base-change map \(\beta\) and open-tensor map \(\gamma\) exist, with the same normalizations, for the ringed diagram topoi of strict coefficient systems; [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison] identifies the realized open adjunction unit and counit with the localized completed ringed-site ones under \(r_j,d_j\). The inverses of \(\beta\) and \(\gamma\) are open adjuncts of pullback/tensor of the open unit, on both sides. Pasting the open-unit square, the pullback and tensor squares of Step 3 and the open-counit square, as in Step 3, gives the coefficient squares for the canonical open base-change and open-tensor isomorphisms. For a proper/open square \(Q\) use \(\Gamma_Q\) and \(\lambda_Q:P_iS_pJ_k\cong S_r\) of [lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting]. By that statement \(\lambda_Q\) is the composite of (a) the right-adjoint conjugate of the cartesian open comparison \(P_pJ_i\cong J_bP_q\), a mate built from \(\beta\) and the \(P\dashv S\) units and counits, (b) \(S_q\) of \(P_bJ_k\cong J_s\), an open base change followed by the open unit, (c) the clopen section formula \(J_s=S_s\), whose map \(J_s\to S_sP_sJ_s\cong S_s\) is a \(P_s\dashv S_s\) unit followed by the inverse open unit, and (d) the direct-image compositor \(S_qS_s\cong S_r\). The integral \(\lambda_{Q,\rm int}\) is the same composite of the completed ringed-site maps. Each factor has a commuting coefficient square by Step 3 and the open case above, and [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] preserves the mate and transposition constructions, so pasting gives the coefficient square for \(\lambda_Q\). Finally \(\Gamma_Q\) is the \(J_i\dashv P_i\) adjunct of \(\lambda_Q^{-1}\), namely \(J_iS_r\to J_iP_iS_pJ_k\to S_pJ_k\) with the open counit, and \(\Gamma_{Q,\rm int}\) is the corresponding open-adjunction transpose; pasting the \(\lambda_Q\) square with the open-counit square gives the square for \(\Gamma_Q\). The intermediate words here may have length four; their comparisons are still the successive composites of the basic \(r_A\), and only the endpoints of the generator are restricted by the statement.

source.place: The sentence “The maps used here are tensor reassociation, evaluation, and adjunction units and counits...”

proof.text: Finally, the proper/open square, open maps, tensor maps, and all the other generators in the statement are actual maps in the same derived-system category. Applying the preceding squares successively to the factors of \(r_B\) and \(r_C\), with the canonical associators and compositors, gives \(\tau_{\mathcal R K_i}\circ r_B=r_C\circ\mathcal R(\tau_{\rm int})\) for every listed generator. The construction uses only the normalized systems and the common finite intervals already assumed; it asserts no arbitrary expression-tree realization, no nested compact-support operation, and no detection of equality by evaluated derived arrows.
